1	# CSR transport audit: ax45mpv_premium
2	
3	Four CSRs audited against AndeStar V5 SPA UM164 V1.7 and the BUILT engine's
4	compiled-in config (the only ground truth for what the engine implements:
5	`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/Vax45mpv_premium/obj_sc/config.inc`, its
6	generated C header `Vax45mpv_premium_config.h`, and
7	`sim_ax45mpv_premium --describe`). No repo files were modified; no builds or
8	simulations were run (`--describe` is an info dump only).
9	
10	PDF page numbers below are absolute PDF pages (451-page file), with the
11	printed page in parentheses where it differs.
12	
13	## Summary
14	
15	| CSR | Addr | Spec existence requirement | Access mode | Premium implements? | Transport on premium? |
16	|-----|------|---------------------------|-------------|--------------------|--------------------|
17	| mcountermask_m | 0x7D1 | `mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1 & misa[20]==1` (U-mode) | Machine (non-standard R/W) | NO (M-only core) | NO - UMODE gate off |
18	| jvt | 0x017 | Zcmt extension implemented (`mrvarch_cfg.Zcmt==1`) | User-level R/W (URW) | NO (no Zcmt) | NO - ZCMT gate off |
19	| mcounterinten | 0x7CF | `mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1` | Machine (non-standard R/W) | YES (perf monitor on) | YES - PERF_MONITOR gate on |
20	| tcontrol | 0x7A5 | Trigger Module (optional) | Machine and Debug (standard R/W) | YES (2 triggers) | YES - TRIGGER gate on |
21	
22	## Engine ground truth (Phase 0)
23	
24	From `build/Vax45mpv_premium/obj_sc/config.inc` (build-directory copy, i.e.
25	what was actually compiled):
26	
27	```
28	161: `define NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS    1        // M-only: misa[20]=0, misa[18]=0
29	176: `define NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR    "yes"
30	177: `define NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT 1        // Andes perf monitor (PMNDS) on
31	193: `define NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT    "yes"         // CoDense (exec.it + uitb) - NOT Zcmt
32	374: `define NDS_NUM_TRIGGER   2                  // trigger module present
33	```
34	
35	No `ZCMT` knob exists anywhere in config.inc (only `NDS_ZCMLSD_SUPPORT 0`,
36	line 126, which is a different Zc feature). The generated
37	`build/Vax45mpv_premium/obj_sc/Vax45mpv_premium_config.h` - the header the
38	caps binding actually reads - mirrors this: `_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS 1`
39	(line 644), `_NDS_NUM_TRIGGER 2` (line 646), `_NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT 1`
40	(line 654), `_NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT 1` (line 166), and no
41	`_NDS_ZCMT_SUPPORT_INT` at all (absent macro reads as "feature off").
42	
43	`sim_ax45mpv_premium --describe` reports the live transported Andes-CSR set:
44	
45	```
46	"andes_csrs": ["mxstatus", "mclk_ctl", "milmb", "mdlmb", "uitb", "pmacfg",
47	  "pmaaddr", "mcountinhibit", "mhpmcounter3..6", "mhpmevent3..6",
48	  "mcounterinten", "mdcause", "tselect", "tdata1", "tdata2", "tcontrol",
49	  "mcontext"]
50	```
51	
52	`mcounterinten` and `tcontrol` are IN; `mcountermask_m` and `jvt` are OUT.
53	(Note `uitb` is in - CoDense is on - while `jvt` is out; see rule 2 below.)
54	
55	## Per-CSR findings
56	
57	### 1. mcountermask_m (0x7D1) - NOT implemented, must NOT transport
58	
59	- **Existence requirement (spec)**: SPA section 9.6.2 "Machine Counter Mask
60	  for M-Mode", PDF p. 339 (printed p. 326):
61	  `IM Requirement: mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1 & misa[20]==1 (User mode implemented)`.
62	  Cross-checked against Table 13 "Summary Table of CSR Existence", PDF p. 45
63	  (printed p. 32): the group {mcounterwen, mcountermask_m, mcountermask_u}
64	  carries `(mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1) & (misa[20]==1) // user`.
65	- **Access mode (spec)**: Machine. `CSR Address: 0x7D1 (non-standard
66	  read/write)` - i.e. MRW, Andes non-standard.
67	- **This engine**: NOT implemented. The PMNDS half is satisfied
68	  (`NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT 1`) but the misa[20] half is not:
69	  `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS 1` means M-only, no U-mode, so the spec's
70	  existence condition is false. This is exactly the documented historical
71	  bug: 0x7D1 was once gated PERF_MONITOR (the PMNDS half only), the caps
72	  over-claimed it on premium, and a Program-Buffer `csrr` faulted cmderr=3,
73	  aborting the CSR sweep (vsim `src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` lines 77-84
74	  comment; skill `references/caps-gating.md` rule 1).
75	- **Transport verdict**: NO on this engine. Correctly gated
76	  `AndesGate::UMODE` (`andes_caps.hpp` case 0x7D1), bound to
77	  `_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2` (`andes_caps_config.hpp` lines 60-62);
78	  premium's value 1 leaves the gate off. Confirmed absent from `--describe`
79	  andes_csrs. The CSR stays in the wire format
80	  (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h:90`, disposition TRANSPORT_NOW in
81	  `tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv`) for U-mode-capable engines; per-engine
82	  caps gating excludes it here.
83	
84	### 2. jvt (0x017) - NOT implemented, must NOT transport
85	
86	- **Existence requirement (spec)**: UM164 V1.7 has NO per-CSR section for
87	  jvt (no `Mnemonic Name: jvt` anywhere in the 451-page text, and no Table 13
88	  row). Its only appearance is Table 10 "RISC-V Standard User Mode CSRs",
89	  PDF p. 43 (printed p. 30), under the group header "ZCE CSRs":
90	  `0x017 | URW | JVT | Table jump base vector and control register`.
91	  jvt is the standard Zcmt table-jump base, so its existence condition is
92	  "Zcmt implemented"; the spec's discoverability bit is `mrvarch_cfg.Zcmt`
93	  (bit [31], RO, reset IM - mrvarch_cfg section, PDF p. 225, Zcmt field on
94	  PDF p. 230): "Indicates if the Zcmt extension is implemented or not."
95	- **Access mode (spec)**: URW - user-level standard read/write (0x017 sits
96	  in the U-mode standard R/W address space; readable/writable from M-mode
97	  too when it exists).
98	- **This engine**: NOT implemented. config.inc carries no Zcmt knob at all
99	  (only `NDS_ZCMLSD_SUPPORT 0`, a different feature), and no
100	  `_NDS_ZCMT_SUPPORT_INT` exists in the generated header. CoDense IS on
101	  (`NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT 1`) but that is the trap for this CSR:
102	  classic Andes CoDense is `exec.it` + `uitb` (0x800) and does NOT imply

compiled-in config (the only ground truth for what the engine implements:
`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/Vax45mpv_premium/obj_sc/config.inc`, its
generated C header `Vax45mpv_premium_config.h`, and
`sim_ax45mpv_premium --describe`). No repo files were modified; no builds or
simulations were run (`--describe` is an info dump only).

PDF page numbers below are absolute PDF pages (451-page file), with the
printed page in parentheses where it differs.

## Summary

| CSR | Addr | Spec existence requirement | Access mode | Premium implements? | Transport on premium? |
|-----|------|---------------------------|-------------|--------------------|--------------------|
| mcountermask_m | 0x7D1 | `mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1 & misa[20]==1` (U-mode) | Machine (non-standard R/W) | NO (M-only core) | NO - UMODE gate off |
| jvt | 0x017 | Zcmt extension implemented (`mrvarch_cfg.Zcmt==1`) | User-level R/W (URW) | NO (no Zcmt) | NO - ZCMT gate off |
| mcounterinten | 0x7CF | `mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1` | Machine (non-standard R/W) | YES (perf monitor on) | YES - PERF_MONITOR gate on |
| tcontrol | 0x7A5 | Trigger Module (optional) | Machine and Debug (standard R/W) | YES (2 triggers) | YES - TRIGGER gate on |

## Engine ground truth (Phase 0)

From `build/Vax45mpv_premium/obj_sc/config.inc` (build-directory copy, i.e.
what was actually compiled):

```
161: `define NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS    1        // M-only: misa[20]=0, misa[18]=0
176: `define NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR    "yes"
177: `define NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT 1        // Andes perf monitor (PMNDS) on
193: `define NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT    "yes"         // CoDense (exec.it + uitb) - NOT Zcmt
374: `define NDS_NUM_TRIGGER   2                  // trigger module present
```

No `ZCMT` knob exists anywhere in config.inc (only `NDS_ZCMLSD_SUPPORT 0`,
line 126, which is a different Zc feature). The generated
`build/Vax45mpv_premium/obj_sc/Vax45mpv_premium_config.h` - the header the
caps binding actually reads - mirrors this: `_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS 1`
(line 644), `_NDS_NUM_TRIGGER 2` (line 646), `_NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT 1`
(line 654), `_NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT 1` (line 166), and no
`_NDS_ZCMT_SUPPORT_INT` at all (absent macro reads as "feature off").

`sim_ax45mpv_premium --describe` reports the live transported Andes-CSR set:

```
"andes_csrs": ["mxstatus", "mclk_ctl", "milmb", "mdlmb", "uitb", "pmacfg",
  "pmaaddr", "mcountinhibit", "mhpmcounter3..6", "mhpmevent3..6",
  "mcounterinten", "mdcause", "tselect", "tdata1", "tdata2", "tcontrol",
  "mcontext"]
```

### 1. mcountermask_m (0x7D1) - NOT implemented, must NOT transport

- **Existence requirement (spec)**: SPA section 9.6.2 "Machine Counter Mask
  for M-Mode", PDF p. 339 (printed p. 326):
  `IM Requirement: mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1 & misa[20]==1 (User mode implemented)`.
  Cross-checked against Table 13 "Summary Table of CSR Existence", PDF p. 45
  (printed p. 32): the group {mcounterwen, mcountermask_m, mcountermask_u}

- **Access mode (spec)**: Machine. `CSR Address: 0x7D1 (non-standard
  read/write)` - i.e. MRW, Andes non-standard.

  existence condition is false. This is exactly the documented historical
  bug: 0x7D1 was once gated PERF_MONITOR (the PMNDS half only), the caps
  over-claimed it on premium, and a Program-Buffer `csrr` faulted cmderr=3,
  aborting the CSR sweep (vsim `src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` lines 77-84

  future Zcmt-configured engine turns it on with zero code change.

### 3. mcounterinten (0x7CF) - implemented, SHOULD transport (and is)

- **Existence requirement (spec)**: SPA section 9.6.5 "Machine Counter
  Interrupt Enable", PDF p. 342 (printed p. 329):
  `IM Requirement: mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1`. Table 13 (PDF p. 45) agrees: the
  {mcounterinten, mcounterovf} group carries `mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1` - the
  Andes performance-monitor feature alone, no privilege-level term.
- **Access mode (spec)**: Machine. `CSR Address: 0x7CF (non-standard
  read/write)` - MRW, Andes non-standard.
- **This engine**: implemented. `NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR "yes"` /
  `_NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT 1` = the PMNDS feature is configured in,
  and the existence condition has no U-mode term, so an M-only core still

  in `csr_coverage.csv`; carried in `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`,
  `state_abi.h:133`). Gated `AndesGate::PERF_MONITOR` (`andes_caps.hpp`
  case 0x7CF, with the explicit comment "PMNDS only"), bound to
  `_NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT` (`andes_caps_config.hpp` lines 38-40) -
  on for premium. Confirmed present in `--describe` andes_csrs, so it is

### 4. tcontrol (0x7A5) - implemented, SHOULD transport (and is)

- **Existence requirement (spec)**: SPA section 6.6.6 "Trigger Control
  Register", PDF p. 154 (printed p. 141):
  `IM Requirement: Trigger Module optional` - it exists only as part of the
  (optional) Trigger Module, and the section text calls it "this optional
  register" even within that module (it is one of two sanctioned solutions
  to M-mode triggers firing inside M-mode trap handlers; fields MTE [3] and
  MPTE [7]). Table 13 does not row tcontrol explicitly; trigger existence
  is probed via the tselect WARL loop (Table 13, PDF p. 46-47).
- **Access mode (spec)**: Machine and Debug. `CSR Address: 0x7A5 (standard

  p. 21) rows it as `0x7A5 | MRW | tcontrol | Trigger control`.
- **This engine**: implemented. `NDS_NUM_TRIGGER 2` (config.inc line 374;

  `NDS_DEBUG_SUPPORT "yes"` - the trigger module is configured with 2
  triggers, and the built engine claims tcontrol in its `--describe`
  andes_csrs card (the claim is sweep-validated by construction: a single
  over-claimed CSR faults the batched Program-Buffer sweep with cmderr=3
  and bisects to name it, so a shipping over-claim cannot survive

- **Transport verdict**: YES. Disposition NEW_TRIG (debug-trigger CSR;

# Carrying scountermask_s (0x9D2) in the hybrid handoff

Answer: scountermask_s is a Supervisor-mode CSR that exists only when
`mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1 & misa[18]==1`, and it is a read/write ALIAS of
mcountermask_s (0x7D2) -- which the handoff ALREADY transports (gated SMODE).
So the state is already carried by the existing wire format; the correct
change is a classifier/doc disposition marking 0x9D2 as alias-covered, not a
new wire field. A separate field is possible (Option B below) but would
double-transport the same physical register. No current engine implements it
anyway: both built engines are M-only.

## 1. Spec facts (AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf)

Source: section 12.3.2 "Supervisor Counter Mask for S-Mode", SPA page 412
(PDF page 425), cross-checked against Table 13 (existence) and Table 14
(aliases).

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Mnemonic | scountermask_s |
| CSR address | 0x9D2 (non-standard read/write) |
| Access Mode | **Supervisor** |
| IM Requirement (existence) | **`mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1 & misa[18]==1`** (Andes perf-monitor extension AND S-mode implemented). Table 13 groups scountermask_m/s/u, scounterinten, scounterovf, scountinhibit, shpmevent3~6 under the same `(mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1) & (misa[18]==1) // supervisor` condition. |
| Reset value | 0 ("The default value of this register is 0.") |
| Fields | CY(0), IR(2), HPM3..HPM6(3..6); bits 7..31 read as 0 |
| Alias | Table 14 "Summary of Aliased CSRs": `mcountermask_s, scountermask_s` -- one physical register, two addresses |
| Write gating | Each bit is READ-ONLY (write silently ignored, no exception) unless the matching bit in mcounterwen (0x7CE) is 1. Not controlled by mcounteren; always readable in S-mode. |

Contrast with the M-mode twin (section 9.6.3, SPA page 326): mcountermask_s,
Access Mode Machine, address 0x7D2, same existence condition
`mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1 & misa[18]==1 (Supervisor mode implemented)`, no
mcounterwen write gating on the M-mode address.

Semantics: setting CY/IR/HPM3~6 stops that counter from incrementing while
the hart is in S-mode.

## 2. Ground truth: no current engine implements it

Per Phase 0, capability comes from the BUILD config.inc, never QEMU:

- `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/Vax45mpv_premium/obj_sc/config.inc`:
  `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS 1` (perf monitor ON)
- `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/Vax46mpv_advanced/obj_sc/config.inc`:
  `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS 1` (perf monitor ON)

Both are M-only, so `misa[18]==0` and scountermask_s does not exist on either
RTL -- a PB `csrr 0x9D2` would fault cmderr=3 and abort the drain CSR sweep.
S-capable cores exist only as unbuilt sources in the vsim checkout
(`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/external/ax66`, `external/ax65`). QEMU DOES
model the CSR (`/home/nick/work/qemu_andesim/target/riscv/andes_csr.c:2314`,
predicate `pmnds_s`, alias handlers `read_scounter`/`write_scounter`) --
another instance of QEMU-exposes != vsim-implements.

## 3. Where it stands in the pipeline today

- Inventory (`tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv`):
  `0x9D2,SRO/SRW,scountermask_s,S-andes,Supervisor Counter Related` -- present.
- Coverage matrix (`tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv:183`): disposition
  **EXCL_MODE** ("S-mode / Hypervisor -- outside the M / M+U envelope"),
  assigned structurally by `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py`.
- The aliased M-mode twin mcountermask_s (0x7D2) is ALREADY in the v4 wire
  format: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h:134`
  (`X(mcountermask_s, 0x7D2, "mcountermask_s")` in `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`),
  gated `AndesGate::SMODE` in the vsim repo
  (`src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp:85`: `case 0x7D2: case 0x7D5: return
  AndesGate::SMODE;`), with SMODE bound to
  `_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 3` in `src/hybrid/andes_caps_config.hpp:63-65`.

Consequence: on any future S-capable engine build, the physical
scountermask_s state already round-trips -- restored via 0x7D2 at resume,
re-read via 0x7D2 at drain, verified via the shared X-macro. The 0x9D2 window
onto it needs nothing on the wire.

## 4. Option A (recommended): document alias coverage, no wire change

Because 0x9D2 and 0x7D2 are one register, the M-mode address is the correct
transport vehicle -- it is writable from the debug/M context unconditionally,
whereas 0x9D2 writes are per-bit dropped when mcounterwen bits are 0 (a
restore-ordering trap the M-address sidesteps entirely).

Touch list (andesim repo only, all offline artifacts):

1. `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py` -- give the Table 14 S-mode aliases a
   distinct disposition (e.g. `EXCL_ALIAS`: "S-mode alias of a transported
   M-mode CSR; state carried via the twin") or, minimally, a comment on the
   EXCL_MODE structural rule naming scountermask_m/s/u, scounterinten,
   scounterovf, scountinhibit, shpmevent3~6 as alias-covered. Never hand-edit
   the CSV.
2. `tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv` -- regenerate through the classifier;
   `tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py` / `test_csr_coverage_complete.sh` must
   stay green (no ABI change, so inventory == matrix == ABI still holds).
3. `docs/csr_coverage.ipynb` legend + `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section 4.4 (per
   project rule: always update USER_GUIDE.md) -- note that S-alias counter
   CSRs are covered via their M-mode twins when the SMODE gate is on.

No vsim change, no ABI bump, no plugin change. Validation: rung 2 of the
ladder (coverage guard) plus one hybrid `--verify` run to confirm nothing
regressed.

## 5. Option B: carry 0x9D2 as its own wire field (what it would take)

Only worth doing as part of the real S/U-envelope work (the handoff today
does not restore any S-mode CSR -- medeleg/mideleg/satp are drained but
deferred). If mandated:

ABI (submodule `andesim_abi`, pinned by BOTH repos):
- `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`: one X-macro line. Note the list is called
  `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST` (M-mode CSRs); an S-mode CSR either gets appended
  there (append-only ordering; bump `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_NUM` 51 -> 52) with a
  comment, or -- cleaner -- starts a new v5 S-mode block with its own
  `HYBRID_FLAG_S_EXT`, since more S CSRs (scounteren, scountinhibit,
  sscratch, ...) would follow. Struct size/offset static asserts in
  `state_abi_check.h` and the vsim `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp` pins
  update with it.
- Bump the submodule pin in andesim (`include/`) AND vsim
  (`external/andesim_abi`) -- two commits, one per repo.

andesim (`/home/nick/work/andesim`):
- `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`: no per-CSR code -- the X-macro resolves the
  gdb name (`"scountermask_s"`; QEMU advertises it, andes_csr.c:2314) and
  drains it (handle setup ~lines 55-68/170-176, drain ~lines 332-355).
- `driver/state_diff.cpp`: compare comes free via the X-macro (~line 147).
  No verify exclusion expected: reset is 0 on both sides and the QEMU alias
  handlers read the same backing store as 0x7D2. The engine's
  `--describe andes_csrs` supported list (the `andes_supported_csr` gate,
  state_diff.cpp:118) must include the new name -- that flows from the vsim
  caps verdict automatically.
- `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py` OVERRIDE map: move `scountermask_s`

  `csr_coverage.csv`; the guard fails loudly until classifier and ABI agree.

vsim (`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim`):
- `src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp`: add `case 0x9D2: return AndesGate::SMODE;`
  with the spec condition in a comment (`PMNDS & misa[18]` -- the privilege

- `src/hybrid/andes_caps_config.hpp`: no change -- SMODE is already bound to

# scountermask_s (0x9D2) transport disposition

## Bottom line

scountermask_s does NOT need its own wire-format field. It is an ALIAS of
mcountermask_s (0x7D2) -- SPA Table 14 lists the pair explicitly -- and
mcountermask_s is already transported (one X-macro line in
`HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`, `include/hybrid/state_abi.h:134`, disposition NEW).
Aliases share one backing register, so restoring/draining via the M-mode name
already round-trips the architectural state that 0x9D2 exposes. The correct
work item is a classification/gating decision inside the future S/U-envelope
work, not a new transport. Today the CSR cannot even exist on either built
engine (both are M-only).

## 1. What the SPA says (AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf)

Per-CSR section 12.3.2 "Supervisor Counter Mask for S-Mode" (doc page 412,
PDF page 425):

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Mnemonic | `scountermask_s` |
| CSR address | 0x9D2 (non-standard read/write) |
| Access Mode | **Supervisor** |
| IM Requirement (existence) | `mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1 & misa[18]==1` (Andes perf monitor present AND S-mode implemented) |
| Reset / default | 0 |
| Semantics | per-counter mask: set CY/IR/HPM3~6 bit -> that counter does not increment in S-mode |

Cross-checks in the consolidated tables:

- **Table 13** (existence conditions, doc pages 32-33 / PDF pages 45-46): the
  group `scountermask_m/s/u`, `scounterinten`, `scounterovf`, `scountinhibit`,
  `shpmevent3~6`, `scountovf` all carry
  `(mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1) & (misa[18]==1) // supervisor`.
- **Table 14** (aliased CSRs, doc page 38 / PDF page 51): row
  `mcountermask_s, scountermask_s` -- the two addresses are one register.
- **Write gating** (sections 9.6.1 and 12.3.2): each bit of scountermask_s is
  read-only when the matching `mcounterwen` (0x7CE) bit is 0; writes to
  read-only bits are silently dropped (no exception). This gating is bound to
  the 0x9D2 alias address -- the M-mode `mcountermask_s` (0x7D2) write path is
  not mcounterwen-gated. It is not controlled by `mcounteren` and is always
  readable in S-mode.

So the answer to "which mode is it": a **Supervisor-mode** CSR (S-andes,
SRO/SRW), existing only when the core has the Andes performance monitor
(PMNDS) and implements S-mode (misa[18], i.e. `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS == 3`
in config.inc terms).

## 2. Where the repos stand today

andesim (`/home/nick/work/andesim`):

- `tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv:183` -- `0x9D2,SRO/SRW,scountermask_s,S-andes,Supervisor Counter Related` (spec snapshot, already present).
- `tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv:183` -- disposition **EXCL_MODE**, produced
  structurally by `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py` (lines 107-108: any
  `S-std`/`S-andes`/`H-std` privilege -> EXCL_MODE, i.e. outside the bare-metal
  M / M+U transport envelope).
- The backing register IS transported: `mcountermask_s` at
  `include/hybrid/state_abi.h:134` in `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`
  (v4 block, `HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT`, `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_NUM == 51`), disposition
  NEW at `csr_coverage.csv:124`. The plugin
  (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:349-354`) drains it by gdb name via the same
  X-macro; `driver/state_diff.cpp:143-148` verify-compares it, skipping names
  absent from the engine's `--describe` `andes_csrs` list.

vsim (`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim`):

- `src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp:85` -- `case 0x7D2: case 0x7D5: return
  AndesGate::SMODE;` (mcountermask_s, mslideleg). There is no case for 0x9D2
  (correct: it is not in any ABI list).
- `src/hybrid/andes_caps_config.hpp:63-65` -- SMODE binds to
  `_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 3`.
- Restore/drain are fully list-driven (`resume_driver.hpp
  restore_andes_m_ext`, `state_drain.hpp drain_andes_m_ext`), including the
  batched Program-Buffer csr sweep; `src/main.cpp:111-116` auto-emits the
  caps-supported names as `--describe` `andes_csrs`.
- Engine ground truth (build-dir `config.inc`, the only truth): both built
  engines are M-only --
  `build/Vax45mpv_premium/obj_sc/config.inc: NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS 1` and
  `build/Vax46mpv_advanced/obj_sc/config.inc: NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS 1`
  (both have `NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR yes`). With misa[18]==0, scountermask_s
  **does not exist** on either; the SMODE gate is off, so even mcountermask_s
  is not swept/verified on them. The S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` (submodule
  `external/ax66` in the vsim checkout) is the engine where PMNDS & misa[18]
  would hold, but it is not currently built (no `build/Vax66_makatau`).
- Shared ABI note: `state_abi.h` lives in the `andesim_abi` submodule, pinned
  by BOTH repos at the same commit (`include/` here == `external/andesim_abi`
  in vsim, both at 1e07582). Any ABI change is a three-repo dance: commit in
  andesim_abi, bump the pin in andesim AND in vsim.

## 3. Recommended plan: no new wire field

1. Keep scountermask_s out of `hybrid_state_v1`. The value already travels as
   `m_ext.mcountermask_s`; a second field would double-transport one register
   and force a write path through the mcounterwen-gated 0x9D2 alias (bits
   silently dropped when the write-enable is clear), while the existing 0x7D2
   restore has no such prerequisite. Restore ordering is already safe: the
   X-macro lists `mcounterwen` (0x7CE) before `mcountermask_s` (0x7D2).
2. When the S/U-envelope work opens (S-mode CSR transport), record the alias
   relationship instead of transporting: either keep EXCL_MODE with a comment,
   or add an explicit `ALIAS` disposition to
   `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py` for the whole Table 14 s*-alias family
   (sstatus, sip, sie, scountermask_m/s/u, scounterinten, scounterovf,
   shpmevent3~6, scountinhibit, scctldata, ...) so the coverage matrix states
   WHY nothing is carried. Regenerate `csr_coverage.csv` through the
   classifier (never by hand); `tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py` +
   `test_csr_coverage_complete.sh` enforce policy == matrix == ABI.
3. Nothing to do in vsim now. Do NOT add `case 0x9D2` to `andes_gate_for`:
   a CSR outside the ABI lists is never swept, and an entry there without a
   transported field is dead spec knowledge.

## 4. If it must be carried explicitly anyway (full touch list)

Only worth doing as part of a real S-envelope feature (e.g. an S-mode ROI that
reads counter masks via the s* alias). Then:

andesim + shared ABI:

- `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (andesim_abi submodule): scountermask_s is
  Supervisor-mode, so it does NOT belong in `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST` ("writable
  M-mode CSR block"). It needs a new appended, flag-gated S-block X-macro list
  (e.g. `HYBRID_S_EXT_CSR_LIST` + `HYBRID_FLAG_S`), following the stability
  rules at the top of the file (append-only; a new optional zero-when-absent
  block can avoid a `HYBRID_STATE_VERSION` bump, else bump 4 -> 5). Then bump
  the submodule pin in both repos. `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp` (vsim)
  pins size/offsets and must be updated.
- `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`: add the S-block drain (same three X-macro
  expansions as M_EXT: handle field, `find_reg` resolve, `read_reg64` +
  flag). Precheck that QEMU's gdbstub for the S-capable cpu (`-cpu andes-ax66`)
  actually advertises `scountermask_s` (dump via RSP
  `qXfer:features:read:riscv-csr.xml`); a missing name resolves NULL and
  drains 0 tolerantly, which --verify would then falsely match (caps rule 3).
- `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py`: override the structural S-andes ->
  EXCL_MODE rule for it (new disposition, e.g. `NEW_SDELTA`, mirroring
  NEW_UDELTA); add the disposition to `check_coverage.py`'s `TRANSPORT` set;
  regenerate `csr_coverage.csv` via the script.
- `driver/state_diff.cpp`: add the S-block compare loop (same
  `andes_verify_excluded` + `andes_supported_csr` gating). No exclusion
  expected: reset default is 0 on both sides, and it is plain state -- but the
  alias means it must always equal `mcountermask_s` in the same drain, a free
  self-consistency check.
- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section 4.4 (what --verify compares) and the vsim
  `ROADMAP.md` known-limits.

vsim:

- TDD RED first: `tests/hybrid/andes_caps.test.cpp` -- extend the `premium()`
  M-only helper (expect `supports_csr(0x9D2) == false`) and an
  ax66_makatau-shaped helper modeled from ITS build config.inc (expect true).
- `src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp`: `case 0x9D2: return AndesGate::SMODE;` with a
  comment citing the spec condition `PMNDS & misa[18]` (caps rule 1: the
  privilege gate is the binding half on current engines, matching how its twin
  0x7D2 is gated). `andes_caps_config.hpp` needs no change (SMODE already
  bound to `_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 3`).
- `src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` / `state_drain.hpp`: new S-block restore/drain
  loops. Restore via the tolerant abstract path; if restore ever writes 0x9D2
  directly, `mcounterwen` must be restored FIRST or the write is silently
  masked (SPA 12.3.2). Better: restore only via 0x7D2 and treat 0x9D2 as
  drain/verify-only. Drain may join the batched PB csr sweep (reads are safe;
  `--describe` `andes_csrs` picks the name up automatically via
  `supported_andes_csr_names`).
- Reset-baseline cache self-invalidates (key includes sim binary mtime+size).

Validation ladder (references/validation.md), on the S/U engine:

2. `bash tests/andes_csr/test_csr_coverage_complete.sh` -- inventory/matrix/ABI

3. Cold-cache hybrid run (`rm -rf ~/.cache/andesim`, then
   `./andesim run --mode hybrid --engine vsim:ax66_makatau --verify ...`) --
   the baseline capture rides the batched PB sweep over the full caps set, so
   one over-claim (e.g. gating 0x9D2 ALWAYS instead of SMODE) aborts with the
   bisected CSR name. This is the only rung that truly validates the gate; a

4. --verify field diffs (expect scountermask_s == mcountermask_s always).

1	# Playbook: raw `exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr=3` at resume on a fresh engine
2	
3	## Answer in one paragraph
4	
5	`cmderr=3` is the RISC-V Debug Spec "exception" code: an instruction inside a
6	Program-Buffer (PB) execution trapped (illegal instruction or load/store
7	access fault) while the hart was halted. The error TEXT is the discriminator
8	(skill: `references/validation.md`, rung 3): the batched CSR sweep bisects its
9	faults and rethrows a RENAMED error (`csr_sweep: CSR 0x... raised cmderr --
10	the caps map over-claims ...`), so a RAW `exec_progbuf: ...` means the fault
11	is in one of the NON-CSR PB sites. On a freshly configured engine the two
12	realistic causes are, in order of likelihood:
13	
14	1. **FP/V flag over-claim from a broken QEMU-side ISA pairing.** The QEMU
15	   fast leg ran a `-cpu` that models F/D and/or V, so the plugin drained
16	   `HYBRID_FLAG_FP` / `HYBRID_FLAG_V`, but the new RTL config has no FPU/VPU.
17	   The engine WARL-pins `mstatus.FS/VS` to Off, and the first `fld`/`fsd` /
18	   `vsetvl`/`vle8.v`/`vse8.v` in a PB raises illegal instruction ->
19	   cmderr=3. Root cause: the hw-config sync chain (engine `config.inc` ->
20	   baked `qemu.cfg` -> `--print-qemu-config` -> QEMU `-readconfig`) is broken
21	   for the fresh engine, so the driver fell back to its default full-featured
22	   `-cpu` (`andes-ax46mpv`).
23	2. **Scratch-page access fault.** Every PB sweep rides the mmap TOP page
24	   (`v_scratch_gpa = ram_base + mem_size`). If the fresh engine's memory map
25	   does not decode that page, the very first sweep (`sd` GPR block-store in
26	   the baseline capture -- runs even on scalar-only handoffs) raises an
27	   access fault -> cmderr=3.
28	
29	A third, less likely cause: the caps map over-claims a CSR AND the sim binary
30	predates the bisect feature (or the batch fault does not reproduce
31	single-CSR), so the error stays raw instead of being renamed.
32	
33	## Why this hits exactly at "resume" on a FIRST run
34	
35	The resume leg (`vsim_andesim/src/simulator.hpp:apply_resume_from_qemu`,
36	lines 208-286) does, in order:
37	
38	1. **Reset-baseline capture** (cold cache -- always cold on a freshly built
39	   engine, the cache key includes the sim binary's mtime+size):
40	   `capture_reset_baseline` (line 349) halts the freshly reset hart, enables
41	   `mstatus.FS/VS` if the incoming flags claim FP/V, then runs a FULL drain
42	   with all sweeps on:
43	   - GPR `sd` block-store sweep (first PB user; `state_drain.hpp` line 95)
44	   - FPR `fsd` sweep (line 109)
45	   - Andes+M-ext `csrr+sd` CSR sweep (line 225) -- faults here get RENAMED
46	   - V `vse8.v` dump sweep LAST (line 263)
47	2. **`ResumeDriver::resume()`** (`resume_driver.hpp` line 146): mstatus
48	   FS/VS enable -> FPR `fld` sweep -> V `vle8.v` sweep + `vsetvl` PB ->
49	   priv/PMP -> Andes/M-ext CSRs (abstract, tolerant; restore-side CSR sweep
50	   is OFF by design) -> GPR `ld` sweep -> counters.
51	
52	So on a fresh engine the fault usually fires inside the baseline capture or
53	the first sweep of `resume()` -- both are "at resume" from the user's view,
54	and both throw out to `main.cpp:544` (`[critical] fatal exception: ...`).
55	
56	Key asymmetry that tells cause 1 from cause 2:
57	- FS/VS-off illegal instruction can only fire in the FPR/V sweeps, and only
58	  when the handoff flags carry FP/V.
59	- A scratch-page access fault fires in EVERY sweep, including the GPR `sd`
60	  sweep of a scalar-only handoff.
61	
62	## Step-by-step triage (read-only, minutes)
63	
64	1. **Confirm the error is raw.** If the message starts `csr_sweep: CSR 0x...`
65	   it is a caps over-claim -- skip to Fix C and the standard caps flow. Raw
66	   `exec_progbuf: ...` -> continue.
67	
68	2. **Confirm the binary has the bisect** (rules out a silent caps
69	   over-claim on an old binary):
70	   ```sh
71	   strings $VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_<engine> | grep -c "csr_sweep: CSR"
72	   ```
73	   `0` -> the binary predates the bisect; a raw cmderr=3 can still be the
74	   caps map. Rebuild from current source before further triage.
75	
76	3. **Read the drained flags** from the handoff file the QEMU leg produced
77	   (the driver's workdir `state-0.bin`, or rerun QEMU1 only). `flags` is a
78	   little-endian u32 at byte offset 8 of `hybrid_state_v1`:
79	   ```sh
80	   od -An -tx4 -j8 -N4 state-0.bin
81	   ```
82	   bit0=RV64, bit1=FP, bit2=V, bit3=ANDES, bit4=M_EXT.
83	
84	4. **Get the engine's ground truth** (skill Phase 0: the BUILD-dir
85	   config.inc is the only truth; never trust QEMU):
86	   ```sh
87	   grep -E "NDS_FPU_TYPE|NDS_VLEN|NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS" \
88	     <vsim>/build/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc
89	   $VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_<engine> --describe
90	   ```
91	
92	5. **Compare.** Flags claim FP but config.inc has no FPU, or flags claim V
93	   but no `NDS_VLEN`/VPU -> **Cause 1 confirmed.** Then check where the
94	   pairing chain broke:
95	   ```sh
96	   $VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_<engine> --print-qemu-config
97	   ```
98	   - Empty output -> the engine was built with an empty `qemu.cfg` blob. The
99	     build log says `No CPU_CONFIG_QEMU_CONVERTER; embedding empty qemu.cfg`
100	     (`vsim_andesim/cmake/VerilatorHelpers.cmake:157-163`) -- typically the
101	     `external/cpu_config_to_march_converter` submodule was never
102	     initialized in the fresh checkout. With an empty probe the andesim
103	     driver keeps the fast leg on its DEFAULT `-cpu andes-ax46mpv`
104	     (`driver/engine_registry.cpp:65`), which models full FP+V.
105	   - Non-empty but wrong (stale ISA, wrong vlen) -> the cfg was generated
106	     from a different config.inc; the engine build dir is out of date.
107	
108	6. **If flags match the engine's caps**, check the scratch page
109	   (**Cause 2**): the driver maps `--mem-size` plus one page; every sweep
110	   targets `ram_base + mem_size .. +4K`. Verify the fresh engine's platform
111	   memory region (its config/YAML, `platform.main_memory.region`) covers
112	   that page for the `--mem-size` used. A region sized exactly to a smaller
113	   RAM, or a different base address, faults every PB load/store. Cheap
114	   cross-check without rebuilds: a scalar fixture (no FP/V flags) faulting
115	   the same way points at the scratch page, not FS/VS.
116	
117	7. **Locate capture vs resume** (refines the diagnosis, optional): if the
118	   log shows `hybrid: reset baseline captured ...` BEFORE the fatal, the
119	   capture succeeded and the fault is in `resume()`; if the fatal comes
120	   first, it died inside the capture drain. `--no-reset-baseline` skips the
121	   capture entirely (the same FPR/V sweeps still run at resume, so a
122	   Cause-1/2 fault only moves, it does not disappear -- itself a useful
123	   signal that this is not a baseline-cache artifact).
124	
125	## The fix
126	
127	### Cause 1: broken QEMU pairing (most likely on a fresh engine)
128	
129	1. In the vsim checkout, initialize the converter and rebuild the engine so
130	   `qemu.cfg` is baked from THIS config.inc:
131	   ```sh
132	   git submodule update --init external/cpu_config_to_march_converter
133	   ./build_vsim.sh    # container build; look for
134	                      # "Generating qemu.cfg for <engine> (andes-<family>)"
135	   ```
136	   (The converter path is the `CPU_CONFIG_QEMU_CONVERTER` cmake cache var,
137	   `VerilatorHelpers.cmake:10-12`; the emitted driver name must match
138	   `-cpu andes-<family>`, family = engine name minus the config suffix.)
139	2. Verify: `sim_<engine> --print-qemu-config` now emits a cfg whose ISA
140	   matches config.inc (no `f`/`d` without an FPU, no `v` without a VPU,
141	   vlen == `NDS_VLEN`).
142	3. Cold-cache rerun (the rebuild self-invalidates the cache anyway, but be
143	   explicit):
144	   ```sh
145	   rm -rf ~/.cache/andesim
146	   ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:<engine> \
147	     --verify tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
148	   ```
149	   The fast leg now runs `-readconfig` with the engine-matched ISA, the
150	   plugin's gdbstub handles for F/V never bind, the flags stay clear, and
151	   no FPR/V sweep is issued.
152	4. Interim workaround only (no rebuild possible): pass an engine-matched
153	   `-cpu` through the post-`--` QEMU args. Do not keep this: the baked
154	   `qemu.cfg` is the single source of truth and survives the next user.
155	
156	### Cause 2: scratch page not decoded
157	
158	Fix the fresh engine's platform memory region so it covers
159	`ram_base .. ram_base + mem_size + 4K` for the intended `--mem-size`, and
160	rebuild; or run with a `--mem-size` small enough that the top page falls
161	inside the engine's decoded RAM. There is no correct workaround that skips
162	the scratch page: GPR/FPR/CSR sweeps fall back to abstract commands only
163	when `*_scratch_fits` fails (a vlenb-driven condition), not on decode
164	errors, and a V handoff requires the page.
165	
166	### Cause 3: caps over-claim (old binary / bisect did not reproduce)
167	
168	Rebuild from current source so the bisect names the CSR, then follow the
169	standard caps flow (skill Phase 3 + `references/caps-gating.md`):
170	1. RED: model the fresh engine's config.inc shape as a helper in
171	   `tests/hybrid/andes_caps.test.cpp` (set exactly the gates its `_NDS_*`
172	   macros turn on) and assert the failing `supports_csr()` verdict.
173	2. GREEN: fix the `case` in `andes_gate_for` (`src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp`)
174	   and, if the gate is new, its `_NDS_*` binding in
175	   `src/hybrid/andes_caps_config.hpp`. Gate on the SPEC's existence
176	   condition exactly, not a correlated feature.
177	3. Rebuild, cold-cache rerun; repeat until the capture is clean. Expect the
178	   `--verify` field count to DROP by one per de-claimed CSR (correct: those
179	   were zero-vs-zero false matches).
180	
181	## After the fix: climb the ladder, then register the engine
182	
183	Validation ladder (`references/validation.md`), bottom-up:
184	1. vsim unit suite (`ctest -LE hybrid-e2e` in the container),
185	2. andesim coverage guard (`bash tests/andes_csr/test_csr_coverage_complete.sh`),
186	3. cold-cache hybrid run with `--verify` (the real caps validator),
187	4. `--verify` field-diff triage (reset-divergent fields -> named exclusions
188	   in `driver/state_diff.cpp`, never to hide transport bugs),
189	5. full e2e matrix (`JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`).
190	
191	A freshly configured engine is a NEW registration by definition (identity =
192	engine name + config.inc hash, `references/engine-registration.md`): produce
193	its CSR manifest, both-direction completeness check, generated
194	write-survival fixtures, and the registration guard entry under
195	`tests/engines/<engine>-<confighash8>/`. Keep a cold-cache hybrid run in the
196	engine's registered test set so this failure class stays a TEST, not an
197	incident.
198	
199	## Evidence trail (files read)
200	
201	- `andesim/.claude/skills/csr-transport-bringup/SKILL.md` + references
202	  (validation.md rung 3 carries the raw-vs-renamed discriminator).
203	- `vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp:183-206` (raw throw site),
204	  `289-341` (csr_sweep bisect + rename; line 335 rethrows raw when no
205	  single CSR reproduces).
206	- `vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp:146-355` (resume order; FS/VS
207	  enable at 172-179; FPR/V/GPR PB sweeps).

# Playbook: raw `exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr=3` at resume on a fresh engine

## Answer in one paragraph

`cmderr=3` is the RISC-V Debug Spec "exception" code: an instruction inside a
Program-Buffer (PB) execution trapped (illegal instruction or load/store
access fault) while the hart was halted. The error TEXT is the discriminator
(skill: `references/validation.md`, rung 3): the batched CSR sweep bisects its
faults and rethrows a RENAMED error (`csr_sweep: CSR 0x... raised cmderr --
the caps map over-claims ...`), so a RAW `exec_progbuf: ...` means the fault
is in one of the NON-CSR PB sites. On a freshly configured engine the two
realistic causes are, in order of likelihood:

1. **FP/V flag over-claim from a broken QEMU-side ISA pairing.** The QEMU
   fast leg ran a `-cpu` that models F/D and/or V, so the plugin drained
   `HYBRID_FLAG_FP` / `HYBRID_FLAG_V`, but the new RTL config has no FPU/VPU.
   The engine WARL-pins `mstatus.FS/VS` to Off, and the first `fld`/`fsd` /
   `vsetvl`/`vle8.v`/`vse8.v` in a PB raises illegal instruction ->
   cmderr=3. Root cause: the hw-config sync chain (engine `config.inc` ->
   baked `qemu.cfg` -> `--print-qemu-config` -> QEMU `-readconfig`) is broken
   for the fresh engine, so the driver fell back to its default full-featured
   `-cpu` (`andes-ax46mpv`).
2. **Scratch-page access fault.** Every PB sweep rides the mmap TOP page
   (`v_scratch_gpa = ram_base + mem_size`). If the fresh engine's memory map
   does not decode that page, the very first sweep (`sd` GPR block-store in
   the baseline capture -- runs even on scalar-only handoffs) raises an
   access fault -> cmderr=3.

A third, less likely cause: the caps map over-claims a CSR AND the sim binary
predates the bisect feature (or the batch fault does not reproduce
single-CSR), so the error stays raw instead of being renamed.

## Why this hits exactly at "resume" on a FIRST run

The resume leg (`vsim_andesim/src/simulator.hpp:apply_resume_from_qemu`,
lines 208-286) does, in order:

1. **Reset-baseline capture** (cold cache -- always cold on a freshly built
   engine, the cache key includes the sim binary's mtime+size):
   `capture_reset_baseline` (line 349) halts the freshly reset hart, enables
   `mstatus.FS/VS` if the incoming flags claim FP/V, then runs a FULL drain
   with all sweeps on:
   - GPR `sd` block-store sweep (first PB user; `state_drain.hpp` line 95)
   - FPR `fsd` sweep (line 109)
   - Andes+M-ext `csrr+sd` CSR sweep (line 225) -- faults here get RENAMED
   - V `vse8.v` dump sweep LAST (line 263)
2. **`ResumeDriver::resume()`** (`resume_driver.hpp` line 146): mstatus
   FS/VS enable -> FPR `fld` sweep -> V `vle8.v` sweep + `vsetvl` PB ->
   priv/PMP -> Andes/M-ext CSRs (abstract, tolerant; restore-side CSR sweep
   is OFF by design) -> GPR `ld` sweep -> counters.

So on a fresh engine the fault usually fires inside the baseline capture or
the first sweep of `resume()` -- both are "at resume" from the user's view,
and both throw out to `main.cpp:544` (`[critical] fatal exception: ...`).

Key asymmetry that tells cause 1 from cause 2:
- FS/VS-off illegal instruction can only fire in the FPR/V sweeps, and only
  when the handoff flags carry FP/V.
- A scratch-page access fault fires in EVERY sweep, including the GPR `sd`
  sweep of a scalar-only handoff.

## Step-by-step triage (read-only, minutes)

1. **Confirm the error is raw.** If the message starts `csr_sweep: CSR 0x...`
   it is a caps over-claim -- skip to Fix C and the standard caps flow. Raw
   `exec_progbuf: ...` -> continue.

2. **Confirm the binary has the bisect** (rules out a silent caps
   over-claim on an old binary):
   ```sh
   strings $VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_<engine> | grep -c "csr_sweep: CSR"
   ```
   `0` -> the binary predates the bisect; a raw cmderr=3 can still be the
   caps map. Rebuild from current source before further triage.

3. **Read the drained flags** from the handoff file the QEMU leg produced
   (the driver's workdir `state-0.bin`, or rerun QEMU1 only). `flags` is a
   little-endian u32 at byte offset 8 of `hybrid_state_v1`:
   ```sh
   od -An -tx4 -j8 -N4 state-0.bin
   ```
   bit0=RV64, bit1=FP, bit2=V, bit3=ANDES, bit4=M_EXT.

4. **Get the engine's ground truth** (skill Phase 0: the BUILD-dir
   config.inc is the only truth; never trust QEMU):
   ```sh
   grep -E "NDS_FPU_TYPE|NDS_VLEN|NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS" \
     <vsim>/build/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc
   $VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_<engine> --describe
   ```

5. **Compare.** Flags claim FP but config.inc has no FPU, or flags claim V
   but no `NDS_VLEN`/VPU -> **Cause 1 confirmed.** Then check where the
   pairing chain broke:
   ```sh
   $VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_<engine> --print-qemu-config
   ```
   - Empty output -> the engine was built with an empty `qemu.cfg` blob. The
     build log says `No CPU_CONFIG_QEMU_CONVERTER; embedding empty qemu.cfg`
     (`vsim_andesim/cmake/VerilatorHelpers.cmake:157-163`) -- typically the
     `external/cpu_config_to_march_converter` submodule was never
     initialized in the fresh checkout. With an empty probe the andesim
     driver keeps the fast leg on its DEFAULT `-cpu andes-ax46mpv`
     (`driver/engine_registry.cpp:65`), which models full FP+V.
   - Non-empty but wrong (stale ISA, wrong vlen) -> the cfg was generated
     from a different config.inc; the engine build dir is out of date.

6. **If flags match the engine's caps**, check the scratch page
   (**Cause 2**): the driver maps `--mem-size` plus one page; every sweep
   targets `ram_base + mem_size .. +4K`. Verify the fresh engine's platform
   memory region (its config/YAML, `platform.main_memory.region`) covers
   that page for the `--mem-size` used. A region sized exactly to a smaller
   RAM, or a different base address, faults every PB load/store. Cheap
   cross-check without rebuilds: a scalar fixture (no FP/V flags) faulting
   the same way points at the scratch page, not FS/VS.

7. **Locate capture vs resume** (refines the diagnosis, optional): if the
   log shows `hybrid: reset baseline captured ...` BEFORE the fatal, the
   capture succeeded and the fault is in `resume()`; if the fatal comes
   first, it died inside the capture drain. `--no-reset-baseline` skips the
   capture entirely (the same FPR/V sweeps still run at resume, so a
   Cause-1/2 fault only moves, it does not disappear -- itself a useful
   signal that this is not a baseline-cache artifact).

## The fix

### Cause 1: broken QEMU pairing (most likely on a fresh engine)

1. In the vsim checkout, initialize the converter and rebuild the engine so
   `qemu.cfg` is baked from THIS config.inc:
   ```sh
   git submodule update --init external/cpu_config_to_march_converter
   ./build_vsim.sh    # container build; look for
                      # "Generating qemu.cfg for <engine> (andes-<family>)"
   ```
   (The converter path is the `CPU_CONFIG_QEMU_CONVERTER` cmake cache var,
   `VerilatorHelpers.cmake:10-12`; the emitted driver name must match
   `-cpu andes-<family>`, family = engine name minus the config suffix.)
2. Verify: `sim_<engine> --print-qemu-config` now emits a cfg whose ISA
   matches config.inc (no `f`/`d` without an FPU, no `v` without a VPU,
   vlen == `NDS_VLEN`).
3. Cold-cache rerun (the rebuild self-invalidates the cache anyway, but be
   explicit):
   ```sh
   rm -rf ~/.cache/andesim
   ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:<engine> \
     --verify tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
   ```
   The fast leg now runs `-readconfig` with the engine-matched ISA, the
   plugin's gdbstub handles for F/V never bind, the flags stay clear, and
   no FPR/V sweep is issued.
4. Interim workaround only (no rebuild possible): pass an engine-matched
   `-cpu` through the post-`--` QEMU args. Do not keep this: the baked
   `qemu.cfg` is the single source of truth and survives the next user.

### Cause 2: scratch page not decoded

Fix the fresh engine's platform memory region so it covers
`ram_base .. ram_base + mem_size + 4K` for the intended `--mem-size`, and
rebuild; or run with a `--mem-size` small enough that the top page falls
inside the engine's decoded RAM. There is no correct workaround that skips
the scratch page: GPR/FPR/CSR sweeps fall back to abstract commands only
when `*_scratch_fits` fails (a vlenb-driven condition), not on decode
errors, and a V handoff requires the page.

### Cause 3: caps over-claim (old binary / bisect did not reproduce)

Rebuild from current source so the bisect names the CSR, then follow the
standard caps flow (skill Phase 3 + `references/caps-gating.md`):
1. RED: model the fresh engine's config.inc shape as a helper in
   `tests/hybrid/andes_caps.test.cpp` (set exactly the gates its `_NDS_*`
   macros turn on) and assert the failing `supports_csr()` verdict.
2. GREEN: fix the `case` in `andes_gate_for` (`src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp`)
   and, if the gate is new, its `_NDS_*` binding in
   `src/hybrid/andes_caps_config.hpp`. Gate on the SPEC's existence
   condition exactly, not a correlated feature.
3. Rebuild, cold-cache rerun; repeat until the capture is clean. Expect the
   `--verify` field count to DROP by one per de-claimed CSR (correct: those
   were zero-vs-zero false matches).

## After the fix: climb the ladder, then register the engine

Validation ladder (`references/validation.md`), bottom-up:
1. vsim unit suite (`ctest -LE hybrid-e2e` in the container),
2. andesim coverage guard (`bash tests/andes_csr/test_csr_coverage_complete.sh`),
3. cold-cache hybrid run with `--verify` (the real caps validator),
4. `--verify` field-diff triage (reset-divergent fields -> named exclusions
   in `driver/state_diff.cpp`, never to hide transport bugs),
5. full e2e matrix (`JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`).

A freshly configured engine is a NEW registration by definition (identity =
engine name + config.inc hash, `references/engine-registration.md`): produce
its CSR manifest, both-direction completeness check, generated
write-survival fixtures, and the registration guard entry under
`tests/engines/<engine>-<confighash8>/`. Keep a cold-cache hybrid run in the
engine's registered test set so this failure class stays a TEST, not an
incident.

## Evidence trail (files read)

- `andesim/.claude/skills/csr-transport-bringup/SKILL.md` + references
  (validation.md rung 3 carries the raw-vs-renamed discriminator).
- `vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp:183-206` (raw throw site),
  `289-341` (csr_sweep bisect + rename; line 335 rethrows raw when no
  single CSR reproduces).
- `vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp:146-355` (resume order; FS/VS
  enable at 172-179; FPR/V/GPR PB sweeps).
- `vsim_andesim/src/simulator.hpp:208-286` (resume leg incl. cold-cache
  baseline capture), `349-393` (capture enables FS/VS then full drain),
  `338-342` (scratch GPA = mmap top page).
- `vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp:95,109,225,263` (drain sweep
  order: GPR sd first, V vse8 last).
- `vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/andes_caps_config.hpp` (gate -> `_NDS_*`
  bindings), `build/V*/obj_sc/config.inc` (ground truth; premium:
  `NDS_FPU_TYPE "dp"`, `NDS_VLEN 512`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS 1`).
- `vsim_andesim/cmake/VerilatorHelpers.cmake:4-12,142-172` (qemu.cfg
  converter gating; empty cfg when converter absent),
  `vsim_andesim/src/main.cpp:35-61,544` (--print-qemu-config; fatal log).
- `andesim/driver/run_plan.hpp:24-73` + `driver/engine_registry.cpp:65`
  (probe -> `-readconfig` staging; empty probe -> default
  `-cpu andes-ax46mpv` fallback).
- `andesim/qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:294-302,361-403` (FP/V flags set
  from what the QEMU gdbstub advertises for the fast-leg -cpu).

2	
3	## Diagnosis (short answer)
4	
5	A Program-Buffer batch faulted on the halted hart. `cmderr=3` is the RISC-V
6	Debug Spec `abstractcs.cmderr` code for "an exception occurred while executing
7	the command": one of the instructions the simulator placed in the Program
8	Buffer raised a hart exception (illegal instruction, or a load/store access
9	fault) while the Debug Module ran it.
10	
11	On a FRESHLY CONFIGURED engine dying AT RESUME, the concrete cause is almost
12	always one of these two, in this order of likelihood:
13	
14	1. **Caps over-claim hit by the CSR sweep during the cold-cache reset-baseline
15	   capture.** A new engine build always misses the reset-baseline cache (the
16	   cache key includes the sim binary's mtime+size --
17	   `vsim src/hybrid/reset_baseline.hpp:21-35`), so the first hybrid run
18	   captures the baseline: a FULL drain of the freshly reset hart
19	   (`vsim src/simulator.hpp:349-393`) with the batched `csrr`+`sd` CSR sweep
20	   enabled (`set_csr_sweep(true)`, simulator.hpp:358). That sweep walks the
21	   COMPLETE caps-supported CSR list, built at compile time from the new
22	   engine's `config.inc` `_NDS_*` macros (`andes_caps_from_config()`,
23	   `src/hybrid/andes_caps_config.hpp`). If the gate map in
24	   `src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` (`andes_gate_for`) over-claims ONE CSR the new
25	   RTL does not implement, the PB `csrr` of it raises illegal instruction ->
26	   cmderr=3 -> `exec_progbuf` throws (`src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp:201-205`)
27	   -> `[critical] fatal exception` (`src/main.cpp:544`). This happens at
28	   resume because the capture runs inside `apply_resume_from_qemu`
29	   (simulator.hpp:208-237), before any state is restored.
30	
31	2. **mstatus.FS/VS Off (or the extension absent) for the FPR/V sweeps.** The
32	   handoff flags come from QEMU's fuller CPU model. If the state carries
33	   `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`/`HYBRID_FLAG_V` but the new engine has no FPU/V at all,
34	   the capture's mstatus enable write WARL-pins FS/VS to 0
35	   (simulator.hpp:359-384) and the subsequent `fsd`/`vsetvl`/`vse8.v` sweep
36	   instructions raise illegal instruction -> the same raw cmderr=3. The
37	   restore-side mirrors (`fld`/`vle8.v` sweeps, the Tier-B `vsetvl` at
38	   `resume_driver.hpp:244`, the PB `csrrw` fallback at
39	   `resume_driver.hpp:452-461`) fault the same way.
40	
41	Rarer third cause: a scratch-page access fault. Every sweep `ld/sd/fld/fsd/
42	vle8/vse8` targets the top page of RAM (`v_scratch_gpa()`,
43	simulator.hpp:338-342). If the new engine's memory map/decoder does not cover
44	that page, the access raises a store/load fault -> cmderr=3 on the very first
45	sweep batch, before any CSR is touched.
46	
47	Key background fact (from the skill's caps-gating notes): the tolerant
48	abstract path MASKS over-claims -- a faulting abstract read mirrors as zero,
49	QEMU drains zero too, and `--verify` falsely matches. Only the batched PB
50	sweep truly validates the caps table, which is exactly why a brand-new engine
51	config fails HERE first: the cold-cache baseline capture is the first thing
52	that runs the sweep over the new caps set.
53	
54	## Why you saw the raw message instead of a named CSR
55	
56	The CSR sweep is self-bisecting: when a batch faults it re-runs one CSR at a
57	time and throws the actionable form
58	(`src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp:318-335`):
59	
60	```
61	csr_sweep: CSR 0x17 raised cmderr -- the caps map over-claims a CSR the hart
62	does not implement (fix andes_caps)
63	```
64	
65	The RAW `exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr=3` surfaces when the
66	faulting PB execution is one the bisector does not wrap:
67	
68	- the GPR `sd` / FPR `fsd` block sweeps of the capture drain
69	  (`pb_block_sweep`, program_buffer.hpp:258),
70	- the V `vsetvl` / grouped `vse8.v`-`vle8.v` sweeps
71	  (program_buffer.hpp:383,396),
72	- the resume-side Tier-B `vsetvl` (resume_driver.hpp:244) or the
73	  one-instruction PB `csrrw` fallback (resume_driver.hpp:460),
74	- or (edge case) the bisect's re-throw when no single CSR reproduces the
75	  batch fault (program_buffer.hpp:335).
76	
77	So the raw message points at the FS/VS-or-extension-absent family or the
78	scratch-page family; the named `csr_sweep: CSR 0x...` message points at a
79	caps over-claim. Step 1 below gets you the discriminating evidence.
80	
81	## Step-by-step fix
82	
83	### Step 1: phase-locate the fault and get the offending name
84	
85	Rerun the exact failing command and keep the full vsim log
86	(`./andesim run --mode hybrid ... 2>&1 | tee /tmp/hybrid.log`).
87	
88	- If the log shows `csr_sweep: CSR 0x... raised cmderr` you already have the
89	  offending CSR's address. Go to Step 3.
90	- If it shows only the raw `exec_progbuf` message, use the surrounding lines:
91	  the info line `hybrid: reset baseline captured -- one-time cost per engine
92	  build + ELF` (simulator.hpp:233-237) prints only AFTER a successful
93	  capture. Error BEFORE that line = fault inside the baseline-capture drain
94	  (FS/VS sweep, scratch page, or a batch the bisect could not reproduce);
95	  error AFTER it = fault inside the restore proper (FPR/V reload sweeps,
96	  Tier-B vsetvl, or the PB csrrw fallback).
97	
98	### Step 2: establish ground truth for the new engine (read-only)
99	
100	The engine's compiled-in config is the ONLY truth about what it implements.
101	Do NOT trust QEMU -- its gdbstub exposes CSRs the vsim RTL lacks.
102	
103	```sh
104	# BUILD-directory copy, not the external/ source tree:
105	grep _NDS_ $VSIM_BIN_DIR/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc | less
106	# e.g. /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc
107	
108	# What the sim binary itself claims to transport:
109	$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_<engine> --describe
110	```
111	
112	Cross-check three things:
113	
114	- Is the fault a caps over-claim? Look up the named CSR's gate in
115	  `vsim src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` (`andes_gate_for`) and its `_NDS_*`
116	  binding in `andes_caps_config.hpp`, then compare against the SPA's IM
117	  Requirement (existence condition) for that CSR. The two historical bugs
118	  are the template: `mcountermask_m` (0x7D1) exists when
119	  `mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1 AND misa[20]==1` but was gated PERF_MONITOR (the PMNDS
120	  half only) and faulted on the M-only premium; `jvt` (0x017) is Zcmt's
121	  table-jump base but was gated CODENSE and faulted on every CoDense core.
122	  Rule: gate on the spec's existence condition EXACTLY; when the condition
123	  needs both a feature and a privilege level, the privilege gate is the
124	  binding one for current engines.
125	- Is it the FS/VS family? Check the config.inc FPU/vector knobs against the
126	  handoff flags (does the paired QEMU `-cpu` model F/D/V the engine lacks?).
127	- Is it the scratch page? Check the engine's RAM region base/size in its
128	  config/YAML against the driver's `--mem-size` (+1 page) mapping.
129	
130	### Step 3: fix the root cause -- no workaround
131	
132	**Caps over-claim (the common case).** Fix the gate in the vsim repo,
133	test-first, per the skill's TDD recipe:
134	
135	1. RED: in `vsim tests/hybrid/andes_caps.test.cpp`, model the NEW engine's
136	   config.inc shape as a caps helper (mirror the existing `premium()`
137	   helper: set exactly the gates its `_NDS_*` macros turn on). Assert the
138	   expected `supports_csr()` verdicts, including
139	   `supports_csr(<offender>) == false`. Build + run in the vsim container
140	   and show the failing assertion:
141	   ```sh
142	   podman run --rm -v /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim:/work -w /work \
143	     localhost/vsim-env:latest \
144	     bash -c 'cmake --build build -j && ctest --test-dir build -LE hybrid-e2e'
145	   ```
146	2. GREEN: move/add the `case` in `andes_gate_for`
147	   (`src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp`) so it encodes the SPA's IM Requirement, and
148	   bind any new gate to its `_NDS_*` macro in `andes_caps_config.hpp`
149	   (an absent macro reads as "off" -- never a compile error, so binding a
150	   not-yet-existing knob is safe). Comment the spec condition at the case.
151	3. Rebuild the sim target; unit suite green.
152	
153	**FS/VS / missing extension.** The capture and resume already force
154	FS/VS to Initial before touching FPRs/V (simulator.hpp:359-384,
155	resume_driver.hpp:172-179); if the write cannot take because the extension
156	does not exist in the RTL, the engine cannot carry that state at all -- the
157	fix is pairing: run the workload on an engine that implements what the QEMU
158	leg drains (or a QEMU `-cpu` matching what the engine implements). Do not
159	patch the sweep to skip faults.
160	
161	**Scratch page.** Fix the engine's memory configuration so the mapped RAM
162	span (including the top transport page) is decodable; this is an engine
163	config bug, not a transport bug.
164	
165	### Step 4: validate with a cold-cache rerun
166	
167	The baseline capture is the caps validator, so force it to re-run:
168	
169	```sh
170	rm -rf ~/.cache/andesim   # force a fresh reset-baseline capture
171	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:<engine> \
172	  --verify tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
173	```
174	
175	(A rebuilt sim binary also self-invalidates the cache -- the key includes
176	its mtime+size -- but clearing the cache makes the rerun unconditional.)
177	
178	A clean capture empirically proves every caps-claimed CSR is csrr-able on
179	this RTL. If another CSR is over-claimed, the run aborts again with the
180	bisected name -- fix that gate the same way and repeat until the capture is
181	clean.
182	
183	**Expected and correct:** the `--verify` compared-field count may DROP by
184	one per de-claimed CSR (premium went 146 -> 144 when 0x7D1 and 0x017 left
185	the set). Those fields were zero-vs-zero false matches before; the drop is
186	the fix working, not a regression.
187

189	
190	```sh
191	# coverage guard (andesim repo): inventory == matrix == ABI
192	bash tests/andes_csr/test_csr_coverage_complete.sh
193	
194	# full e2e matrix
195	QEMU_BIN_DIR=... VSIM_BIN_DIR=... VSIM_QEMU=... VSIM_QEMU32=... \
196	VSIM_PLUGIN=/home/nick/work/andesim/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so \
197	JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
198	```

# cmderr=3 at resume on a freshly configured engine: diagnosis + playbook

## Diagnosis (short answer)

A Program-Buffer batch faulted on the halted hart. `cmderr=3` is the RISC-V
Debug Spec `abstractcs.cmderr` code for "an exception occurred while executing
the command": one of the instructions the simulator placed in the Program
Buffer raised a hart exception (illegal instruction, or a load/store access
fault) while the Debug Module ran it.

On a FRESHLY CONFIGURED engine dying AT RESUME, the concrete cause is almost
always one of these two, in this order of likelihood:

1. **Caps over-claim hit by the CSR sweep during the cold-cache reset-baseline
   capture.** A new engine build always misses the reset-baseline cache (the
   cache key includes the sim binary's mtime+size --
   `vsim src/hybrid/reset_baseline.hpp:21-35`), so the first hybrid run
   captures the baseline: a FULL drain of the freshly reset hart
   (`vsim src/simulator.hpp:349-393`) with the batched `csrr`+`sd` CSR sweep
   enabled (`set_csr_sweep(true)`, simulator.hpp:358). That sweep walks the
   COMPLETE caps-supported CSR list, built at compile time from the new
   engine's `config.inc` `_NDS_*` macros (`andes_caps_from_config()`,
   `src/hybrid/andes_caps_config.hpp`). If the gate map in
   `src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` (`andes_gate_for`) over-claims ONE CSR the new
   RTL does not implement, the PB `csrr` of it raises illegal instruction ->
   cmderr=3 -> `exec_progbuf` throws (`src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp:201-205`)
   -> `[critical] fatal exception` (`src/main.cpp:544`). This happens at
   resume because the capture runs inside `apply_resume_from_qemu`
   (simulator.hpp:208-237), before any state is restored.

2. **mstatus.FS/VS Off (or the extension absent) for the FPR/V sweeps.** The
   handoff flags come from QEMU's fuller CPU model. If the state carries
   `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`/`HYBRID_FLAG_V` but the new engine has no FPU/V at all,
   the capture's mstatus enable write WARL-pins FS/VS to 0
   (simulator.hpp:359-384) and the subsequent `fsd`/`vsetvl`/`vse8.v` sweep
   instructions raise illegal instruction -> the same raw cmderr=3. The
   restore-side mirrors (`fld`/`vle8.v` sweeps, the Tier-B `vsetvl` at
   `resume_driver.hpp:244`, the PB `csrrw` fallback at
   `resume_driver.hpp:452-461`) fault the same way.

Rarer third cause: a scratch-page access fault. Every sweep `ld/sd/fld/fsd/
vle8/vse8` targets the top page of RAM (`v_scratch_gpa()`,
simulator.hpp:338-342). If the new engine's memory map/decoder does not cover
that page, the access raises a store/load fault -> cmderr=3 on the very first
sweep batch, before any CSR is touched.

Key background fact (from the skill's caps-gating notes): the tolerant
abstract path MASKS over-claims -- a faulting abstract read mirrors as zero,
QEMU drains zero too, and `--verify` falsely matches. Only the batched PB
sweep truly validates the caps table, which is exactly why a brand-new engine
config fails HERE first: the cold-cache baseline capture is the first thing
that runs the sweep over the new caps set.

## Why you saw the raw message instead of a named CSR

The CSR sweep is self-bisecting: when a batch faults it re-runs one CSR at a
time and throws the actionable form
(`src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp:318-335`):

```
csr_sweep: CSR 0x17 raised cmderr -- the caps map over-claims a CSR the hart
does not implement (fix andes_caps)
```

The RAW `exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr=3` surfaces when the
faulting PB execution is one the bisector does not wrap:

- the GPR `sd` / FPR `fsd` block sweeps of the capture drain
  (`pb_block_sweep`, program_buffer.hpp:258),
- the V `vsetvl` / grouped `vse8.v`-`vle8.v` sweeps
  (program_buffer.hpp:383,396),
- the resume-side Tier-B `vsetvl` (resume_driver.hpp:244) or the
  one-instruction PB `csrrw` fallback (resume_driver.hpp:460),
- or (edge case) the bisect's re-throw when no single CSR reproduces the
  batch fault (program_buffer.hpp:335).

So the raw message points at the FS/VS-or-extension-absent family or the
scratch-page family; the named `csr_sweep: CSR 0x...` message points at a
caps over-claim. Step 1 below gets you the discriminating evidence.

### Step 1: phase-locate the fault and get the offending name

Rerun the exact failing command and keep the full vsim log

  offending CSR's address. Go to Step 3.
- If it shows only the raw `exec_progbuf` message, use the surrounding lines:

  capture. Error BEFORE that line = fault inside the baseline-capture drain
  (FS/VS sweep, scratch page, or a batch the bisect could not reproduce);
  error AFTER it = fault inside the restore proper (FPR/V reload sweeps,
  Tier-B vsetvl, or the PB csrrw fallback).

### Step 2: establish ground truth for the new engine (read-only)

The engine's compiled-in config is the ONLY truth about what it implements.
Do NOT trust QEMU -- its gdbstub exposes CSRs the vsim RTL lacks.

```sh

grep _NDS_ $VSIM_BIN_DIR/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc | less
# e.g. /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc

# What the sim binary itself claims to transport:
$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_<engine> --describe
```

- Is the fault a caps over-claim? Look up the named CSR's gate in
  `vsim src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` (`andes_gate_for`) and its `_NDS_*`
  binding in `andes_caps_config.hpp`, then compare against the SPA's IM
  Requirement (existence condition) for that CSR. The two historical bugs

  table-jump base but was gated CODENSE and faulted on every CoDense core.
  Rule: gate on the spec's existence condition EXACTLY; when the condition
  needs both a feature and a privilege level, the privilege gate is the
  binding one for current engines.
- Is it the FS/VS family? Check the config.inc FPU/vector knobs against the
  handoff flags (does the paired QEMU `-cpu` model F/D/V the engine lacks?).
- Is it the scratch page? Check the engine's RAM region base/size in its
  config/YAML against the driver's `--mem-size` (+1 page) mapping.

### Step 3: fix the root cause -- no workaround

**Caps over-claim (the common case).** Fix the gate in the vsim repo,
test-first, per the skill's TDD recipe:

1. RED: in `vsim tests/hybrid/andes_caps.test.cpp`, model the NEW engine's
   config.inc shape as a caps helper (mirror the existing `premium()`
   helper: set exactly the gates its `_NDS_*` macros turn on). Assert the
   expected `supports_csr()` verdicts, including
   `supports_csr(<offender>) == false`. Build + run in the vsim container
   and show the failing assertion:
   ```sh
   podman run --rm -v /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim:/work -w /work \
     localhost/vsim-env:latest \
     bash -c 'cmake --build build -j && ctest --test-dir build -LE hybrid-e2e'
   ```
2. GREEN: move/add the `case` in `andes_gate_for`
   (`src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp`) so it encodes the SPA's IM Requirement, and
   bind any new gate to its `_NDS_*` macro in `andes_caps_config.hpp`
   (an absent macro reads as "off" -- never a compile error, so binding a
   not-yet-existing knob is safe). Comment the spec condition at the case.
3. Rebuild the sim target; unit suite green.

**FS/VS / missing extension.** The capture and resume already force
FS/VS to Initial before touching FPRs/V (simulator.hpp:359-384,
resume_driver.hpp:172-179); if the write cannot take because the extension
does not exist in the RTL, the engine cannot carry that state at all -- the
fix is pairing: run the workload on an engine that implements what the QEMU
leg drains (or a QEMU `-cpu` matching what the engine implements). Do not
patch the sweep to skip faults.

**Scratch page.** Fix the engine's memory configuration so the mapped RAM
span (including the top transport page) is decodable; this is an engine
config bug, not a transport bug.

### Step 4: validate with a cold-cache rerun

The baseline capture is the caps validator, so force it to re-run:

```sh
rm -rf ~/.cache/andesim   # force a fresh reset-baseline capture
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:<engine> \
  --verify tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
```

(A rebuilt sim binary also self-invalidates the cache -- the key includes
its mtime+size -- but clearing the cache makes the rerun unconditional.)

A clean capture empirically proves every caps-claimed CSR is csrr-able on
this RTL. If another CSR is over-claimed, the run aborts again with the
bisected name -- fix that gate the same way and repeat until the capture is
clean.

**Expected and correct:** the `--verify` compared-field count may DROP by
one per de-claimed CSR (premium went 146 -> 144 when 0x7D1 and 0x017 left
the set). Those fields were zero-vs-zero false matches before; the drop is
the fix working, not a regression.

Then climb the rest of the ladder:

```sh
# coverage guard (andesim repo): inventory == matrix == ABI
bash tests/andes_csr/test_csr_coverage_complete.sh

# full e2e matrix
QEMU_BIN_DIR=... VSIM_BIN_DIR=... VSIM_QEMU=... VSIM_QEMU32=... \
VSIM_PLUGIN=/home/nick/work/andesim/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so \
JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
```

### Step 5: commit and document

Tidy First: the caps fix (with its test) is one behavioral commit on a green
suite. Update the vsim `ROADMAP.md` known-limits and andesim
`docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section 4.4 if the verify-compared set changed; refresh
`tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv` through the classifier
(`scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py`), never by hand.

## What NOT to do

- **Do not disable the CSR sweep** (`set_csr_sweep(false)`) or fall back to
  abstract-only transport to make the run pass. The sweep is the only thing
  that validates the caps table; the tolerant abstract path mirrors a
  faulting read as zero and `--verify` false-matches zero==zero -- both
  historical caps bugs were "verified" for months this way.
- **Do not catch/clear the cmderr and continue.** A partially executed PB
  batch leaves the hart state partially restored/drained, which is worse
  than the abort (this is why `exec_progbuf` throws by design,
  program_buffer.hpp:177-181).
- **Do not widen caps to `AndesCaps::all()`** or gate off a whole feature to
  dodge one CSR -- fix the one gate to the spec's existence condition.
- **Do not turn ON the restore-side CSR sweep** while debugging: it is off
  by design (simulator.hpp:266-272) because a `csrrw` to a read-only or
  WARL-illegal field faults the batch with no idempotent retry story.
- **Do not exclude the CSR in `driver/state_diff.cpp`** -- verify exclusion
  is only for engine-reset divergences (msp_bound/msp_base, milmb/mdlmb
  enable bit, mip timer bit), never to hide a transport/caps bug.

## Appendix: cmderr decode and fault-site map

| baseline capture drain | `vsetvl` + `vse8.v` dump sweep | no V / VS pinned Off |
| baseline capture drain | `csrr`+`sd` CSR sweep | caps over-claim (bisected -> named error) |
| restore | `vsetvl` + `vle8.v` reload sweep | no V / VS pinned Off |
| restore | Tier-B `vsetvl x0,x5,x6` | no V |
| restore | FPR `fld` sweep, GPR `ld` sweep | no FPU / scratch page |
