# Engine registration: CSR test artifacts required to ship a new vsim engine

Answer: four deliverables per engine BUILD -- (1) a CSR manifest, (2) a
both-direction completeness check, (3) generated per-engine write-survival
fixtures, (4) a registration guard -- all keyed by the hash of the build's
`config.inc`, so a rebuild with a different config is a NEW registration by
construction and can never silently reuse the old artifacts.

## 1. The identity: an engine build = (core, config)

The engine's compiled-in config is the only truth about which CSRs it
implements. The registration key is the engine name plus a short hash
(first 8 hex chars) of the BUILD-directory config:

```
$VSIM_BIN_DIR/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc
```

Concretely, with today's `config.env` (`VSIM_BIN_DIR=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build`):

- `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/Vax45mpv_premium/obj_sc/config.inc`
- `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/Vax46mpv_advanced/obj_sc/config.inc`

Use the build copy, never the `external/` source tree (it can differ from
what was actually built), and never QEMU's view (its gdbstub advertises CSRs
the vsim RTL does not implement; sweeping one stalls or faults the Debug
Module).

Artifact layout in the andesim repo:

```
tests/engines/<engine>-<confighash8>/
|-- engine.env          # engine name, QEMU -cpu pairing, march, vlen, priv levels
|-- csr_manifest.csv    # deliverable 1
`-- fixtures/           # deliverable 3 (generated)
```

Rebuilding the same core with a different config changes the hash, which
changes the directory name, which makes the guard (deliverable 4) refuse to
run the engine against the old artifacts. "Same core, new config" cannot be
silently reused -- reuse is impossible by construction, not by review
discipline.

## 2. Deliverable 1: the CSR manifest (`csr_manifest.csv`)

One row per spec-inventory CSR -- ALL of them (the current inventory,
`tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv`, has 232 CSRs from the SPA), not just
the transported ones:

```
addr,name,access,exists_cond,implemented,transported,gate_or_disposition,reset_value
0x7D1,mcountermask_m,MRW,PMNDS&misa[20],no,no,UMODE(off),-
0x7CF,mcounterinten,MRW,PMNDS,yes,yes,PERF_MONITOR,0x0
```

Each column comes from a DIFFERENT source, and they must agree:

- `exists_cond`: the SPA spec (per-CSR IM Requirement / Table 13) --
  Phase 1 output.
- `implemented`: EMPIRICAL, from the probe (section 3) -- never inferred
  from QEMU.
- `transported`: the caps verdict of THIS binary --
  `sim_<engine> --describe` emits the `andes_csrs` JSON list the engine
  compiled in (`src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` + `andes_caps_config.hpp` in the
  vsim repo).
- `reset_value`: EMPIRICAL -- from the probe or the reset-baseline capture
  (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/*.bin` is a `hybrid_state_v1` struct; parse with
  the ABI header `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`). This IS the engine's reset
  value table: generated, reviewed once by a human against the spec's reset
  column (IM/DC fields will differ from the spec -- expected and fine), then
  committed.

## 3. Deliverable 2: the both-direction completeness check

"Nothing missed" has two failure directions; each needs its own check.

**Over-claim** (caps says yes, RTL says no): the batched Program-Buffer CSR
sweep faults (cmderr=3) on a single over-claimed CSR and bisects to name it.
This matters because the tolerant abstract-command path MASKS this bug: a
faulting read mirrors as zero, QEMU drains zero too, and `--verify` falsely
matches. A cold-cache hybrid run exercises the sweep via the reset-baseline
capture -- keep one in the engine's registered test set so an over-claim is
a TEST failure, not a field incident.

**Under-claim** (RTL implements it, caps gates it off -- the silent
state-loss case): script it from the manifest. Every row whose
`exists_cond` evaluates true against this `config.inc` (or whose probe says
`implemented == yes`) must have `transported == yes` OR a named `EXCL_*`
disposition from the coverage matrix (`tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv`).
A row with neither FAILS the script. No human list-checking.

**The probe** that feeds both: a checked read of every inventory CSR on the
halted, freshly reset hart. The DM mirrors an unimplemented CSR as a
cmderr, which `read_register_64_checked` reports as nullopt -- so one pass
(~232 reads, seconds of sim time) yields the implemented set AND the
empirical reset values. EXCL_SIDEFX rows (reads with side effects) are
skipped by policy. The sim binaries have no probe mode today (grep of
`src/hybrid/` and `main.cpp` in the vsim repo finds none); building it is
part of the FIRST registration -- a small loop over the inventory using the
existing DM helpers, done test-first.

## 4. Deliverable 3: generated per-engine write-survival fixtures

Write-survival tests must come from a GENERATOR keyed by the manifest, not
from hand-written files. Today's CSR fixtures (`tests/fixtures/
rt_csr_survival.S`, `rt_m_ext_counters.S`, `rt_m_ext_trigcause.S`) are
hand-written and engine-generic; hand-written sets rot and miss CSRs when a
new engine claims a different set.

For each transported read/write CSR the generator emits: a distinctive
write BEFORE the ROI (proves resume restores it into the vsim hart) and one
INSIDE the ROI (proves drain captures it), asserted via the drained state
and `--verify`.

The generator needs a per-CSR safe-write policy, because blind writes to
control CSRs break the run (`mcache_ctl` flips caches, `milmb`/`mdlmb`
move local memory, `mhsp_ctl` arms stack protection). Three tiers:

- plain state (scratch-like, masks, event selects): full distinctive pattern;
- WARL-constrained: write within a reviewed mask;
- dangerous control CSRs: skip-list with a comment saying why -- their
  round-trip is still covered by `--verify` on real workload values.

The policy table is reviewed once and committed next to the generator.

## 5. Deliverable 4: the registration guard

A script that cross-checks: every engine that `./andesim list engines`
reports (driver F2 discovery, `driver/cmd_list.cpp:list_engines`) must have
a `tests/engines/<engine>-<confighash8>/` directory whose hash matches the
CURRENT binary's `config.inc`, with the manifest and generated fixtures
present. An unregistered engine, or one whose hash went stale after a
rebuild, fails with "run the bring-up registration". Wire it next to the
existing coverage guard (`tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py` /
`test_csr_coverage_complete.sh`) so CI runs both.

## 6. How the checks compose ("nothing missed" as machine invariants)

Layered guards, each catching what the others cannot:

1. `tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py` (exists today): inventory == matrix
   == ABI (`state_abi.h` X-macros `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST` /
   `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`). A CSR added to the wire format without a
   disposition, or vice versa, fails loudly. Engine-independent.
2. `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_caps_parity.sh` +
   `scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py` (exist today): the offline Python
   gate logic run on the engine's build `config.inc` must reproduce the
   built binary's `--describe andes_csrs` list -- offline config == compiled
   caps.
3. The under-claim script (deliverable 2, per engine): implemented-but-not-
   transported-and-not-excluded fails.
4. The cold-cache sweep run (deliverable 2, per engine): over-claims fault
   and name the CSR.
5. The registration guard (deliverable 4): unregistered or stale-hash
   engines cannot run at all.
6. Named verify exclusions live in ONE place
   (`driver/state_diff.cpp:andes_verify_excluded`, currently e.g.
   `msp_bound`/`msp_base`, `milmb`/`mdlmb`, `mip`), each with a comment
   naming the engine-reset divergence. Exclusion is only for
   engine-implementation artifacts, never to hide a transport bug.

Rebuild-with-different-config is covered by check 5: the new `config.inc`
hashes differently, the old `tests/engines/` dir no longer matches, and
every engine-scoped artifact (manifest, probe results, fixtures) must be
regenerated and re-reviewed under the new key.

## 7. Matrix runner integration

The full ~47-fixture suite stays on the default engines (wall-time). Every
REGISTERED engine runs its own core set on every suite run: the probe
check, its generated CSR fixtures, one cold-cache hybrid run (the sweep
validator), and one `--verify` run. `scripts/run_e2e.sh` takes the engine
axis from the registration dirs -- today it hardcodes a canonical default
engine plus an S/U special case for the priv fixtures, so this is a change
to make during first registration. After that, adding a registration
automatically adds its tests: no runner edit, nothing to forget.

## 8. Current state and first-registration work list

Exists today (andesim repo):

- `tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` (232 CSRs), `csr_coverage.csv`,
  `check_coverage.py`, `test_csr_coverage_complete.sh`
- `scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py`, `classify_csr_coverage.py`,
  `config_inc_to_andes_caps.py`, `render_csr_matrix.py`
- `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_caps_parity.sh`
- `driver/state_diff.cpp` named exclusions; reset-baseline cache under
  `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/`
- vsim side: `--describe` with `andes_csrs`, caps gates in
  `src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` / `andes_caps_config.hpp`

Missing -- to build (test-first) as part of the FIRST registration:

1. `tests/engines/` layout + `engine.env` convention (does not exist yet).
2. The probe mode in the sim binary (checked read of the full inventory on
   the reset hart).
3. The manifest generator (probe output + `--describe` + spec inventory ->
   `csr_manifest.csv`).
4. The under-claim completeness script.
5. The fixture generator + reviewed safe-write policy table.
6. The registration guard script, wired next to the coverage guard.
7. `run_e2e.sh` engine axis from registration dirs.

Then register both currently built engines (`ax45mpv_premium`,
`ax46mpv_advanced`) as the first two entries; any future build -- new core
OR new config of an old core -- follows the same recipe and is refused by
the guard until its artifacts exist.

# CSR test artifacts required to ship a new vsim engine

Answer: an engine is shippable when six artifact groups exist and are green --
(1) the engine's `--describe andes_csrs` self-report, (2) the vsim caps unit
tests that model its config shape, (3) the andesim offline deriver + parity
flywheel entry for it, (4) the spec/matrix/ABI coverage guard, (5) its
`--verify` exclusion entries with named divergences, and (6) the empirical
validation ladder results (cold-cache PB CSR sweep, `--verify`, e2e).
"Nothing missed" is enforced by three machine checks (coverage guard, parity
flywheel, batched CSR sweep) plus one self-invalidating cache; a rebuild with
a different config is absorbed automatically by everything except the unit-test
config models, which must be updated by hand. Audit status as of 2026-07-02:
the parity flywheel currently FAILS and is not wired into `test_all.sh` --
details in "Gaps found" below.

Repos: andesim = `/home/nick/work/andesim`, vsim = `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim`.
Engines present in the build: `sim_ax45mpv_premium` (shipping),
`sim_ax46mpv_advanced` (the new build; adds PowerBrake + StackSafe over premium).

---

## 1. The artifact checklist (what must exist, per engine)

### A. Engine self-report (vsim binary)

- `sim_<engine> --describe` must print the descriptor JSON with the
  `andes_csrs` array (contract: `andesim/docs/engine_interface.md`; parsed
  into `EngineDescriptor.andes_csrs` by `andesim/driver/engine_descriptor.hpp`).
  This list is computed at runtime by `hybrid::supported_andes_csr_names()`
  from `andes_caps_from_config()` (`vsim/src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` +
  `andes_caps_config.hpp`), i.e. from the engine's compiled-in `_NDS_*`
  macros. The andesim driver uses it to gate which Andes/M-ext CSRs
  `--verify` compares (`driver/state_diff.cpp`, `andes_supported_csr`), so a
  wrong list silently mis-scopes verification. Verified live: both engines
  emit it (`ax46mpv_advanced` reports 27 names).
- The engine's embedded build config,
  `vsim/build/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc`. This file, not the `external/`
  source tree, is the ONLY capability ground truth (observed divergence:
  built premium has perf-monitor + PMA on while its `external/` config.inc
  has them off). Every other artifact derives from it.

### B. Caps unit tests (vsim repo, run via ctest in the container)

- `vsim/tests/hybrid/andes_caps.test.cpp`: a helper that models THIS
  engine's config shape (pattern: `premium()` sets exactly the `AndesGate`s
  its config.inc turns on) plus `supports_csr()` verdict assertions,
  including the CSRs the engine must NOT claim (the hang/fault cases). Per
  the skill's TDD recipe, a new engine gets its own helper (e.g.
  `advanced()`); the helper is the machine-checked record of the engine
  shape.
- `vsim/tests/hybrid/andes_caps_config.test.cpp`: unit-tests the
  `_NDS_*` macro -> gate binding with controlled `#define`s. Needs a new
  case only if the engine introduces a config knob not yet bound in
  `andes_caps_config.hpp` (absent macro reads as "off", never a compile
  error -- but an unbound knob means the feature's CSRs stay gated off).
- `vsim/tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp` (engine-independent): pins the
  wire-format size/offsets; re-run, must be untouched unless the CSR lists
  grew.

### C. Offline deriver + parity flywheel (andesim repo)

- `andesim/scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py`: the Python mirror of the
  C++ gate logic. It must produce, from the engine's build config.inc, the
  byte-identical list the engine's `--describe` reports.
- `andesim/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_caps_parity.sh`: the drift guard that
  asserts exactly that (offline deriver(build config.inc) == runtime
  `--describe andes_csrs`). A new engine needs its own entry here -- today
  the script hardcodes `sim_ax45mpv_premium` and
  `Vax45mpv_premium/obj_sc/config.inc`, so `ax46mpv_advanced` is not covered
  by any parity check.

### D. Spec / matrix / ABI coverage set (andesim repo, engine-independent)

These are per-spec, not per-engine, but must be regenerated and green before
shipping (and refreshed if the new core family comes with a new SPA revision):

- `tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` -- the spec snapshot (232 CSRs), from
  `scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py <SPA.pdf>`.
- `tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv` -- per-CSR transport disposition, from
  `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py` (never hand-edited; legend in its
  docstring: TRANSPORT_NOW / NEW / NEW_TRIG / NEW_UDELTA / CONST_RO /
  EXCL_*).
- `tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py` + `test_csr_coverage_complete.sh` --
  the guard: (A) matrix covers exactly the inventory, (B) re-running the
  classifier reproduces the committed matrix, (C) ABI
  (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` X-macro lists) transports only
  matrix-approved CSRs and every carried-today CSR is in the ABI.
  Verified live today: PASS ("232 CSRs classified, matrix==policy").
- `docs/csr_coverage.ipynb` -- the human-review rendering, regenerated by
  `scripts/render_csr_matrix.py` (names the test that covers each done CSR).

### E. Verify-exclusion entries (andesim repo)

- `driver/state_diff.cpp`, `andes_verify_excluded`: any CSR whose
  QEMU-vs-engine RESET value legitimately diverges on this engine must be
  listed WITH a comment naming the divergence (precedents: msp_bound /
  msp_base all-ones-vs-zero, milmb/mdlmb enable bit, mhpmcounter3-6 tick
  during the ROI, mdcause HW-set, tdata1/tcontrol/mcontext WARL defaults).
  A new engine can both ADD entries (new divergent CSR it implements, e.g.
  advanced now implements msp_bound/msp_base for real -- already excluded)
  and make existing ones re-checkable. Exclusion is only for
  engine-implementation artifacts, never to hide a transport bug.
- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section 4.4 must document what `--verify` compares
  and excludes for the engine.

### F. Empirical validation results (the ladder, per engine)

1. vsim unit suite (`ctest -LE hybrid-e2e` in the container).
2. Coverage guard (`bash tests/andes_csr/test_csr_coverage_complete.sh`).
3. Cold-cache hybrid run -- THE caps validator:
   `rm -rf ~/.cache/andesim && ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker
   --engine vsim:<engine> --verify tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf`.
   The reset-baseline capture is a FULL drain whose CSR block rides the
   batched Program-Buffer `csr_sweep` over the COMPLETE caps-claimed list,
   so a clean capture empirically proves every claimed CSR is csrr-able on
   this RTL; one over-claim aborts with the bisected CSR name
   ("csr_sweep: CSR 0x17 raised cmderr -- the caps map over-claims...").
4. `--verify` PASS with the expected field count (a count DROP after
   de-claiming a CSR is correct: those were zero-vs-zero false matches).
5. Full e2e matrix (`JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`); if the engine is
   S/U-capable, map the fixtures that need it (pattern:
   `scripts/run_e2e.sh` pins `rt_priv_smode`/`rt_priv_umode` to
   `sim_ax66_makatau` + `QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66`).
- Plus a captured reset baseline under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/` -- not a
  committed artifact, but its existence after step 3 is the proof the sweep
  ran clean for this exact build.

---

## 2. How "nothing is missed" is enforced (the guard lattice)

Four independent mechanisms; each catches what the others cannot:

1. **X-macro single source of truth.** Every transported Andes/M-ext CSR is
   one line in `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST` / `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`
   (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`); plugin drain, resume, drain re-read,
   `--describe`, and verify all iterate the same list, so no consumer can
   drift. Pitfall it does NOT cover: a list CSR with no case in
   `andes_gate_for()` defaults to ALWAYS = claimed on every engine.
2. **Coverage guard** (`check_coverage.py`): inventory == matrix == ABI.
   Catches a spec CSR with no disposition, an ABI CSR the matrix excludes,
   a carried CSR dropped from the ABI, and hand-edits that the classifier
   policy does not reproduce. NEW/NEW_* CSRs not yet in the ABI surface as
   PENDING (backlog), so the guard tightens automatically as features land.
3. **Parity flywheel** (`test_andes_caps_parity.sh`): the offline Python
   gate model fed the engine's OWN embedded build config.inc must equal the
   runtime `--describe`. Catches gate-logic drift between the two repos.
4. **Batched PB csr_sweep at cold-cache capture**: the only EMPIRICAL check
   against the RTL. Critical because the tolerant abstract path MASKS
   over-claims (a faulting read mirrors as zero, QEMU drains zero for a
   never-written CSR, `--verify` false-matches zero == zero -- two real bugs,
   jvt and mcountermask_m, were "verified" for months this way). The sweep
   faults on one over-claim and bisects to name the CSR.

Under-claims (CSR implemented but gated off) show up as `--verify`
mismatches when a fixture writes the CSR -- which is why the e2e fixtures
that exercise the CSR sections (e.g. `handoff_roundtrip.S`,
`rt_csr_survival`, the F5 counter fixture) are part of the ship gate, not
optional.

---

## 3. Rebuild of the same core with a different config

What tracks the rebuild automatically:

- **`--describe andes_csrs`**: recompiled from the new `cpu_config.hpp`
  (`andes_caps_from_config()`), so the runtime claim always matches the new
  build. The andesim driver re-reads it per run (engine discovery spawns
  `--describe`), so verify-gating follows automatically.
- **The parity test**: re-derives from `build/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc`
  on every run -- the exact blob the binary embeds -- so a config flip
  (premium's perf-monitor/PMA on-vs-off case) is absorbed, and only genuine
  gate-LOGIC drift fails it.
- **The reset-baseline cache**: keyed
  `<engine>-<version>-<bin mtime>-<bin size>-<elf mtime>-<elf size>.bin`
  (`vsim/src/hybrid/reset_baseline.hpp`), so any rebuild self-invalidates
  the cache; the next hybrid run re-captures the baseline, which re-runs
  the full CSR sweep over the NEW claimed set -- the empirical validator
  re-fires for free. A corrupt/stale entry means "capture again", never an
  aborted run.
- **Liveness-gate correctness**: the baseline is per (engine build, ELF),
  so restore-skipping never compares against another config's reset values.

What does NOT track the rebuild (manual, must be on the ship checklist):

- The unit-test config models: `andes_caps.test.cpp`'s per-engine helper
  and `andes_caps_config.test.cpp`'s `#define` block are point-in-time
  snapshots. Rule from the skill: when the engine's config changes, fix the
  helper to match the new config.inc -- it is the reviewed record of the
  engine shape. Live example of the rot: `andes_caps_config.test.cpp` still
  models premium with perf-monitor/PMA OFF while the built premium has them
  ON (the built config diverged from the external source the test was
  written against).
- The `--verify` exclusion list: a config flip can change which CSRs are
  reset-divergent (e.g. turning StackSafe on makes msp_bound/msp_base real
  registers). Re-run rung 4 and re-justify each exclusion comment.
- `run_e2e.sh` fixture-to-engine pinning, if the rebuild changes the
  privilege envelope.

---

## 4. Gaps found in this audit (live, 2026-07-02)

1. **The parity flywheel FAILS right now.** vsim commits `a0357df`
   (mcountermask_m 0x7D1: PERF_MONITOR -> UMODE) and `292a560` (jvt 0x017:
   CODENSE -> ZCMT) fixed the C++ gates and the rebuilt engines report the
   corrected list, but `andesim/scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py` still
   maps `("mcountermask_m", "PERF_MONITOR")` and `("jvt", "CODENSE")` (and
   its `gates()` has no ZCMT entry). Ran it: offline claims
   `mcountermask_m` + `jvt` on both premium and advanced; `--describe`
   (correctly) does not. The flywheel is doing its job -- the andesim-side
   deriver needs the same two gate fixes before either engine ships.
2. **The parity test never runs in the suite.** `scripts/test_all.sh`'s
   contract phase globs `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh` and
   `tests/andes_csr/test_*.sh`; `test_andes_caps_parity.sh` matches
   neither, so the failing flywheel sat unnoticed. Wire it into the glob
   (or rename it to match) so drift is caught on every `test_all.sh`.
3. **The parity test is single-engine.** It hardcodes premium's binary and
   config.inc path. For the new `ax46mpv_advanced` (and each future
   engine/config) it should loop over every `sim_*` +
   `V*/obj_sc/config.inc` pair under `VSIM_BIN_DIR` -- that also makes
   "same core, different config" a zero-maintenance case.
4. **Stale unit-test config model** (see section 3): the
   `andes_caps_config.test.cpp` premium macro block no longer matches the
   built premium's config.inc. Harmless as a binding test, but it has
   stopped being the record of the real engine shape; update it (and add an
   advanced-shaped helper to `andes_caps.test.cpp`) when registering the
   new engine.

## 5. Ship checklist (condensed, per new engine build)

1. Read `build/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc` (never `external/`); note the
   `_NDS_*` deltas vs the last shipped config.
2. If a delta has no gate binding, add gate + binding + macro-level test
   (TDD: failing expectation first) in the vsim repo.
3. Add/refresh the engine's caps helper + verdicts in
   `andes_caps.test.cpp`; ctest green in the container.
4. Update `scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py` if gate logic changed; add
   the engine to `test_andes_caps_parity.sh`; parity green.
5. Coverage guard green (`test_csr_coverage_complete.sh`); refresh
   inventory/matrix/notebook only if the SPA revision changed.
6. `rm -rf ~/.cache/andesim`, cold-cache hybrid `--verify` run on the new
   engine: clean sweep (no cmderr bisect), `--verify` PASS, record the
   field count.
7. Review `andes_verify_excluded` against the new config; add/remove
   entries with named divergences; update USER_GUIDE 4.4.
8. Full e2e matrix green (`JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`), with fixture
   pinning if the privilege envelope changed.
9. Separate commits (Tidy First): caps fixes, deriver/parity updates, doc
   updates -- each on a green suite.
